conditions.description: Run yt-dlp custom match filter on returned info and apply options.
conditions.info1: Filtering is based on yt-dlp's --match-filter logic. Any expression that works with yt-dlp will also work here, including the same boolean operators. We added extended support for the OR ( {'||'} ) operator, which yt-dlp does not natively support. This allows you to combine multiple conditions more flexibly.
conditions.info2: The primary use case for this feature is to apply custom cli arguments to specific returned info.
conditions.info3: For example, i follow specific channel that sometimes region lock some videos, by using the following filter i am able to bypass it availability = 'needs_auth' & channel_id = 'channel_id'. and set proxy for that specific video, while leaving the rest of the videos to be downloaded normally.
conditions.info4: The data which the filter is applied on is the same data that yt-dlp returns, simply, click on the information button, and check the data to craft your filter. You will get instant feedback if the filter matches or not.

notificationsPage.description: Send notifications to your webhooks based on specified events or presets.
notificationsPage.info1: When you export notification target, We remove Authorization header key by default, However this might not be enough to remove credentials from the exported data. it's your responsibility to ensure that the exported data does not contain any sensitive information for sharing.
notificationsPage.info2: When you set the request type as Form, the event data will be JSON encoded and sent as ...&data_key=json_string, only the data field will be JSON encoded. The other keys id, event and created_at will be sent as they are.
notificationsPage.info3: We also send two special headers X-Event-ID and X-Event with the request.
notificationsPage.info4: If you have selected specific presets or events, this will take priority, For example, if you limited the target to default preset and selected ALL events, only events that reference the default preset will be sent to that target. Like wise, if you have limited both events and presets, then ONLY events that satisfy both conditions will be sent to that target. Only the test events can bypass these conditions.

status.monitoringDisabledDesc: Enable resource monitoring by setting YTP_MONITOR_ENABLED=true.
status.helpAppCpu: App CPU - CPU usage of the YTPTube process tree, including worker subprocesses, normalized against the effective core count.
status.helpSystemCpu: System CPU - Overall system-wide CPU usage across all cores.
status.helpRss: RSS (Resident Set Size) - Physical memory (RAM) held by the app process tree, including shared libraries.
status.helpUss: USS (Unique Set Size) - Memory pages exclusive to this process. Excludes shared libraries, a truer measure of consumption.
status.helpHandles: Handles - Open file descriptors (files, sockets, pipes). Rapid growth may indicate a resource leak.
status.helpDiskIo: Disk I/O - System-wide disk read/write throughput from the host. This is not limited to YTPTube or its worker subprocesses.
status.helpChildren: Child Processes - Sub-processes like ffmpeg, yt-dlp, or browsers. Their resource usage is included in app totals and listed separately because they often dominate total load.
status.helpPool: Pool - Paused means no new downloads start; Running means workers are accepting new items.
status.helpBottlenecks: Bottlenecks - Analyses the last 30 samples for CPU, memory, I/O, or network contention. The summary describes the issue; details include measurements from the sample window.
